mainTopic: How much property must a שכיב מרע keep for himself so that his gift stays valid even if he recovers, and whether the word 'קרקע' in a משנה always means only land
overview: The משנה taught that if a שכיב מרע (a person on his deathbed) gave away his property but kept 'any amount of land' for himself, the gift stays valid even if he gets better. The גמרא asks how much 'any amount' really means. רב says he must keep land that is enough to live on. רב ירמיה בר אבא says even movable property is enough, as long as he can live on it. רבי זירא praises both views, because either way the man kept something to rely on if he recovers. רב יוסף objects that the משנה says 'land,' not movables, and 'any amount,' not 'enough to live on.' אביי answers by asking whether 'land' in a משנה always means only land. He brings a משנה about a master who writes all his property over to his slave, and that proof continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: The משנה: keeping any land keeps the gift valid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line from the משנה it is about to discuss: if the שכיב מרע kept any amount of land, his gift stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he kept any amount of land for himself, his gift stands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the earlier משנה so it can ask about it. This step sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שכיב מרע who gives away everything is assumed to be giving only because he expects to die, so if he recovers the gift is cancelled. But if he kept some land, he was clearly not giving everything away because of death, so the gift stays valid even if he recovers.

keyTerms.meaning: He kept back, he left over for himself
Land, real estate
Any amount at all, even a tiny bit
His gift stands, it stays valid

phrases.english: If he kept back any amount of land,
phrases.notes: This is the שכיב מרע from the משנה on 146b, a person on his deathbed who gave his property away.

phrases.english: his gift stands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the discussion by quoting the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If a שכיב מרע kept any land for himself, his gift is valid even if he recovers.

steps.title: How much is 'any amount'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what amount the משנה means by 'any amount.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the exact meaning of 'any amount' in the משנה. The next two steps give the answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Any amount' sounds like even a tiny piece is enough. The גמרא suspects there is a real minimum, because a tiny piece does not show that he planned to live on what he kept.

keyTerms.meaning: And how much?

phrases.english: And how much is "any amount"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of a phrase in the quoted משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What minimum amount the משנה means by 'any amount'

steps.title: רב: land enough to live on
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה reports in the name of רב that the person must keep land that is enough to support him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: land that is enough for his livelihood.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question. 'Any amount' really means enough land to support himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב, a tiny scrap is not enough. Only land that could support him shows that he kept something to live on and meant the rest as a real gift.

keyTerms.meaning: Enough for his livelihood, enough to support him
רב יהודה reporting a teaching of his teacher רב

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
Land that is enough for his livelihood.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He must keep land that is enough to support him.

steps.title: רב ירמיה בר אבא: even movables enough to live on
steps.stepSummary: רב ירמיה בר אבא says that even movable property, if it is enough to support him, keeps the gift valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ירמיה בר אבא said: movable property that is enough for his livelihood.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives a different answer. He says it does not have to be land; movable things are also fine, as long as they are enough to live on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He agrees with רב that the amount must be enough for a livelihood. He goes further by saying the kind of property does not matter, so movables count too.

keyTerms.meaning: Movable property, such as money or goods, as opposed to land

phrases.english: And Rav Yirmeya bar Abba said:
Movable property that is enough for his livelihood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a broader second answer to the same question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Even movable property is enough, as long as it can support him.

steps.title: רבי זירא praises both teachings as well reasoned
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא says both teachings make good sense. If he recovers, he can rely on what he kept, whether it is land or movables.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: How carefully aimed are the teachings of the elders! What is the reason for land? Because if he recovers, he can rely on it. Movables too: if he recovers, he can rely on them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא explains the reasoning behind both answers and praises them. Whatever he kept is something to live on if he gets better.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key idea is that he kept something to fall back on. That idea explains why the amount must be enough to live on, and it also explains why movables can work just as well as land.

keyTerms.meaning: Carefully aimed, precise
The teachings of the elders
If he gets up, meaning if he recovers
He relies on it

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
How carefully aimed are the teachings of the elders!
phrases.notes: The 'elders' are רב (as reported by רב יהודה) and רב ירמיה בר אבא.

phrases.english: Land, what is the reason?
Because if he recovers, he relies on it.
Movables too:
if he recovers, he relies on them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the reasoning that supports both answers
steps.mimraCoreRuling: What matters is that he kept something to live on if he recovers, so land or movables both work.

steps.title: רב יוסף: both views clash with the משנה's wording
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף challenges the praise. The משנה says 'land,' which goes against the movables view, and it says 'any amount,' which goes against the 'enough to live on' requirement.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objected: What is so precise about it? The one who says movables, but we learned 'land'! The one who says enough for his livelihood, but we learned 'any amount'!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף attacks both teachings because they do not fit the words of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the משנה literally. 'Land' should mean land only, so movables should not count. 'Any amount' should mean even a tiny bit, so there should be no 'livelihood' minimum.

keyTerms.meaning: He objected to it, he challenged it
Precision, careful aim

phrases.english: Rav Yosef objected to it:
And what is so precise about it?
The one who says movables:
phrases.notes: That is רב ירמיה בר אבא.

phrases.english: we learned "land"!
The one who says enough for his livelihood:
we learned "any amount"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the teachings that רבי זירא praised
steps.kashyaTarget: The teachings of רב and רב ירמיה בר אבא, and רבי זירא's praise of them
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The plain words 'land' and 'any amount' in the משנה go against allowing movables and against requiring a livelihood minimum.

steps.title: אביי: does 'land' always mean only land?
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers רב יוסף with a question: is it true that wherever a משנה says 'land' it means only land?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: And wherever it teaches 'land,' does it mean specifically land?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רב יוסף's literal reading of the word 'land.' This sets up a proof from another משנה in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף assumed that 'land' must mean only land. אביי challenges that assumption and suggests the word may not always be meant that strictly.

keyTerms.meaning: Anywhere, wherever
Specifically, exactly, strictly

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
And wherever it teaches "land,"
does it mean specifically land?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's objection by questioning his assumption
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The part of רב יוסף's objection that rests on the word 'land'
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumes that 'land' in a משנה always means land only.

steps.title: אביי's source: the משנה about writing property to a slave
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a משנה: a master who writes all his property to his slave frees him, but if he kept any land, the slave is not freed. רבי שמעון says the slave is always freed unless the master says 'except for one ten-thousandth.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't we learn: One who writes all his property to his slave, the slave goes free. If he kept any amount of land, the slave does not go free. רבי שמעון says: He is always free, unless the master says, 'All my property is given to so-and-so my slave, except for one ten-thousandth of it.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a משנה that also uses the words 'kept any amount of land' to back up his question. The גמרא shows how this proves his point on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the master kept something back, maybe he kept the slave himself, so the slave is not freed. The same wording, 'any amount of land,' appears here, and אביי will use this משנה to show that 'land' is not always meant strictly. רבי שמעון holds that only a clear 'except for' statement keeps the slave from going free.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn in a משנה? Used to bring a source
He went out a free man, he was freed
Always, in every case
Except for one part out of ten thousand

steps.confusionAlert: The quote stops before אביי explains his proof, so do not decide yet how it answers רב יוסף. The גמרא makes that point on the next עמוד.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn:
One who writes all his property to his slave,
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in פאה 3:8. 'Writes' means he gives it over in a written document.

phrases.english: the slave goes out a free man.
If he kept back any amount of land,
the slave does not go out a free man.
Rabbi Shimon says:
He is always a free man,
unless the master says:
"All my property is given to so-and-so my slave,
except for one ten-thousandth of it."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source that supports אביי's question
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that 'land' in a משנה does not always mean land only
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in פאה 3:8 about a master who writes all his property to his slave
